title: Target Sum Index Pair Problem

content.problemStatement:
You receive an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`. The task is to find two distinct elements in the array whose sum equals `target`, and output their zero-based indices.

Important details:
- Each input is guaranteed to have exactly one valid answer.
- An element may be used no more than once.
- Either order of the two returned indices is acceptable.
- The array may contain negative values, zero, and duplicate values.
- The solution must run in expected O(n) time with O(n) auxiliary space.

Design an efficient algorithm that meets these requirements.
constraints: Exactly one valid answer exists for each input
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of arguments: [nums, target]. Example: [[2,7,11,15], 9]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialized return value: [index1, index2]
notes: Any valid order of the two indices is acceptable.
Solutions that rely on sorting the array must preserve original indices; preferred approach is hash map.

sampleTestCases.explanation: nums[0] = 2 and nums[1] = 7. Their sum is 9, so [0, 1] is correct.
nums[1] = 2 and nums[2] = 4. They add to 6, so [1, 2] is valid.
Both occurrences of 3 are needed: nums[0] + nums[1] = 6. Indices are distinct, so [0, 1] is valid.

hidden.label: Long zeros with pair at ends (concrete)
Large ordered array with pair near end
Negative and positive mix with unique complement
Repeated small numbers with single valid pair

notes: Every hidden test case is concrete and uses zero-based indices.
The checker must accept either order of the two valid indices.
Inputs are constructed so exactly one valid index pair exists per test case.

solution.approach: Single-pass hash map: iterate once, for each number compute complement = target - num, check if complement exists in map; if yes return [map[complement], current_index]; otherwise store current number -> index. This yields O(n) time and O(n) space.
notes: Do not sort the array in-place because indices must refer to original positions.
Carefully handle duplicates: store the first occurrence index and ensure the complement lookup uses a previously seen index when appropriate.

bruteForce.description: Check every pair of indices (i, j) with i < j and return the pair whose values sum to target. This is O(n^2) and fails the expected time requirement for large n.

better.description: Sort a copy of the array with original indices and use two pointers to find the pair. Sorting costs O(n log n) and requires preserving original indices; this approach is acceptable but not optimal for the expected O(n) requirement.
better.complexity: Time O(n log n), Space O(n).

optimal.description: Use a hash map to record seen values and their indices while scanning once. For each value v at index i, check if target - v is already in the map; if so, return the stored index and i. This is O(n) time and O(n) space.

hints: Iterate once and store seen values in a hash map mapping value -> index.
For each element, compute complement = target - value and check the map before inserting the current value.
Be careful with duplicates: store the first occurrence index so later duplicates can pair with earlier values.
followUps: How would you adapt the solution if multiple pairs could be returned (return all unique index pairs)?
How would you modify the approach to return indices in sorted order or to handle streaming input where the array is too large to store?
learningObjectives: Use hash maps for O(n) lookups
Handle duplicates and edge cases in array problems
Design single-pass algorithms with correct index tracking
